newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Troops storm Lebanese-owned store in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Troops storm Lebanese-owned store in Sierra Leone.

text.p: Troops stormed a Lebanese-owned store in the Sierra Leone capital on Tuesday after a soldier on patrol in the area was shot in the foot, witnesses said.
Soldiers fired volleys of automatic weapons into the three-storey building in central Freetown, which serves as a store and home to the Lebanese shopowner, they said.

The store in Kissy street in the mostly deserted business district is one of a few still run by the handful of Lebanese remaining in the city. Most of Freetown's 5,000 Lebanese community fled the looting and violence that followed a May 25 army coup.
"Soldiers attacked the house claiming that their colleague was shot from there," one witness said.
It was not clear who had fired at the soldier.
The upper floors of the building were riddled with bullet holes while several soldiers took positions in the store front.
There was no immediate word on the fate of the shopkeeper.

The shooting following clashes on Monday between soldiers and students demonstrating against military rule. People ventured cautiously into the streets to see what was going on, before running back home.
Most of the few shops that have reopened since the looting in May remained closed on Tuesday after shutting their doors at the start of Monday's unrest in which a student was killed.

State radio said the youth was killed by gunfire and that at least 35 people were arrested when troops clashed with students demanding the return of ousted president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who is exiled in Guinea.
The students held their march in defiance of a ban by the military junta led by Major John Paul Koroma.
Witnesses said the clash took place outside the Sierra Leone Nursing School in the centre of the capital, where students had taken refuge.
State radio said troops broke up a similar protest march by students in the southern provincial capital Boh on Monday, but it gave no account of casualties or arrests.
State radio said only seven of the 35 arrested in Freetown were students.
The toppling of Kabbah, just over a year after he won elections ending four years of military rule, has been condemned by the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.

The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has imposed a land, sea and air blockade on Sierra Leone. Troops of its Nigerian-led military wing, ECOMOG, have clashed repeatedly with junta soldiers and their rebel allies.
